issues.legal_issue: A court that had jurisdiction when a personal suit was instituted retains jurisdiction when the defendant dies and non-resident legal representatives are substituted to defend the claim in their representative capacity.
material_facts: The money suits were instituted against defendants who resided within the jurisdiction of the court, which was competent to try them when filed.
While the suits were pending, one defendant died and non-resident relatives who held parts of his property were added as his legal representatives.
The representatives defended the claim on behalf of the deceased, and any recovery against them was limited to the deceased’s assets in their hands.
The present suit sought to enforce the resulting foreign judgments.
issues.conclusion: The court’s jurisdiction and the competence of the suits remained unaffected by the defendant’s death and the substitution of non-resident legal representatives; the judgments were pronounced by a court of competent jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a foreign judgment is conclusive unless, among other exceptions, it was not pronounced by a court of competent jurisdiction. The private international law rule limiting jurisdiction over personal actions against non-residents is assessed when the suit is instituted; it does not invalidate a suit that was competent at its inception merely because non-resident legal representatives are later substituted. Sections 52 and Order XXII, rule 4(2), of the Code reflect that the claim continues against the deceased’s estate and that representatives defend in their representative capacity. The court considered Sirdar Gurdyal Singh v. The Raja of Faridkote, Emmanuel v. Symon, Schibsby v. Westenholz, Travers v. Holley, Dunne v. Saban, Mountbatten v. Mountbatten, and Dulles v. Vidler, and held that the cited execution decisions in Kanchamalai Pathar v. Ry. Shahaji Rajah Saheb and Erava v. Sidramappa Pasare did not govern this question.

rule.if: foreign_judgment_enforcement_case and suit_competent_when_instituted and defendant_died_during_suit and nonresident_representatives_substituted and representatives_defended_in_representative_capacity

predicates.foreign_judgment_enforcement_case: The proceeding seeks to enforce a judgment given by a court outside the enforcing forum.
predicates.suit_competent_when_instituted: The original suit was properly brought before a court that had jurisdiction over the defendant when the suit was instituted.
predicates.defendant_died_during_suit: A defendant died while the original suit was pending.
predicates.nonresident_representatives_substituted: Persons who did not reside within the court’s jurisdiction were added to the pending suit as the deceased defendant’s representatives.
predicates.representatives_defended_in_representati: The substituted persons defended the claim on behalf of the deceased, with their liability confined to the deceased’s assets in their hands.

issues.definition: When a foreign judgment is sought to be enforced and the original suit was competent at filing, the defendant’s death and substitution of non-resident representatives defending only in that capacity do not end the original court’s jurisdiction.

issues.legal_issue: A person who receives only part of a deceased person’s estate under a will may be a legal representative of the deceased’s estate.
material_facts: Several persons were joined in the earlier suits as legal representatives because they held different parts of the deceased’s property under a settlement deed and a registered will.
The persons holding property under the will argued that receiving only part of the estate did not make them legal representatives.
The court concluded that the estate need not be represented by a single person holding the whole estate.
issues.conclusion: Legatees who receive separate portions of a deceased person’s estate under a will are included among legal representatives; the estate need not mean the whole estate.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(11) of the Code of Civil Procedure defines a legal representative to include a person who in law represents the estate of a deceased person and a person who intermeddles with the estate. The definition includes legatees of separate portions of an estate, just as it includes persons who intermeddle with part of the estate. The court relied on the reasoning in Dinamoni Chaudhurani v. Elahandut Khan and disapproved the contrary observation in Natesa Sastrigal v. Alamelu Achi.

predicates.estate_claim_against_successors: A claim concerning a deceased person’s estate is brought against persons said to represent that estate.
predicates.persons_received_separate_estate_portion: Different persons received separate portions of the deceased person’s estate under a will.

issues.definition: When a claim concerning a deceased person’s estate is brought against successors, persons who received separate portions under a will count as legal representatives.
